name: GLB improvement 3: live adaptive best-of-N and report fix
description: Offline tooling to confirm the imp-ops-2 finding out of sample: sampling until the first valid and assembled candidate matched best-of-3 (100% valid, 87.5% assembled) at 1.6 samples per brief in simulation. Add a brief-id filter to the generator and bench, a script that lists briefs still lacking a good candidate, jobs for fresh seeds 4 to 6 where seeds 5 and 6 only run on the remaining briefs, and fix the report so assembly-repair rows show the repaired assembled values (imp-ops-2 found they do not).
standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Build and test with fixtures, fake HTTP servers on localhost and temp dirs. Never call the real Ollama, never run the benchmark, never read or write runs/, data/, out/ or eval/, never edit briefs, bench/glb/eval_subjects.json or prompts/. Never commit. Assembly stays a quality signal, never a validity failure reason. Never type the literal completion tag except when every criterion holds.
readFirst: runs/ is off limits; read ralph/imp-ops-2 notes in .ralph-tui/progress.md for the report defect
scripts/glb_best_of.py (candidates_for skips ids a run lacks; keep that)
manualGates: Owner reviews and commits the imp-3 diff
Owner runs ralph/imp-ops-3.prd.json (local only, about 90 minutes)
Owner approves any rented-GPU spend; Ralph never creates pods

stories.title: Assembly repair writes assembly.jsonl and the report shows it
stories.description: As the owner, I want the after-assembly-repair report rows to carry the repaired assembled values, because imp-ops-2 showed they silently kept the originals.
steps: In scripts/glb_repair.py (mode assembly), after validating the repaired rows, write RUN_DIR/repair-asm/assembly.jsonl with one line {id, kind, assembly} per repaired id, taken from each new validation row's stats.glb.assembly (kind from the original assembly.jsonl entry or the brief); null when the row is not ok. Keep validation.jsonl untouched.

In scripts/glb_report.py the '<model> after assembly repair' row must read assembled values for repaired ids from repair-asm/assembly.jsonl (fall back to the validation rows' stats.glb.assembly), and original values elsewhere.

Tests: a fixture run with 4 ok rows, 2 unassembled; a repair-asm dir where one id becomes assembled and one stays not; assert the report row's assembled count and 'of all briefs' share change accordingly (fails on the old behaviour).
criteria: The report test asserts assembled count goes from 2 to 3 of 4 on the fixture
glb_repair writes repair-asm/assembly.jsonl for repaired ids (asserted)

stories.title: Brief id filter in the generator and bench
stories.description: As an operator, I want a later seed to run only on the briefs that still need a sample.
steps: Add `--ids-file FILE` (one brief id per line, blank lines and # comments ignored) to scripts/teacher_generate.py: only briefs whose id is listed are generated; unknown ids print a warning; existing raw files are still skipped.
Add the same `--ids-file` to scripts/glb_bench.py, forwarded to teacher_generate.py; the validator step must only see the raw files that exist (it already walks the raw dir).
Tests: teacher_generate with a 5-brief fixture and a 2-id file requests exactly those 2 (fake server request count); an unknown id warns; glb_bench builds the command with --ids-file for a dry run.
criteria: Fake-server test asserts exactly the listed ids are requested
glb_bench --dry-run prints a command containing --ids-file=<path> when given (use the = form)
Without the flag nothing changes (existing tests pass)

stories.title: List briefs that still lack a good candidate (glb_adaptive_ids.py)
stories.description: As an operator, I want the list of briefs with no valid and assembled candidate yet across the runs so far.
steps: Create scripts/glb_adaptive_ids.py --runs DIR [DIR ...] --briefs FILE --out FILE [--no-compute]: for each brief id in briefs, keep it when no run has a row that is ok and assembled (kind-aware assembly.jsonl, computed with glb_assembly.mjs when missing unless --no-compute, reuse the helper glb_best_of.py uses). Write one id per line to --out and print 'remaining X of Y'.

Tests with a 3-run, 6-brief fixture: ids already good in run 1 are dropped, ids good only in run 2 are dropped when run 2 is given, ids with no ok candidate or only unassembled candidates stay; a run directory with no validation.jsonl is an error.
criteria: A run with no assembly.jsonl and --no-compute counts its rows as not assembled with a printed warning

stories.title: imp_ops.sh jobs for fresh seeds 4 to 6
stories.description: As an operator, I want fixed commands for the live adaptive run.
steps: Add jobs to scripts/imp_ops.sh: `ad4` runs the bench on all 48 briefs with `--seed 4 --run-suffix=-s4`; `ad5` runs it with `--seed 5 --run-suffix=-s5 --ids-file=runs/imp/adaptive/ids_after_s4.txt`; `ad6` with `--seed 6 --run-suffix=-s6 --ids-file=runs/imp/adaptive/ids_after_s5.txt`. All use --only glimmer-v3 and --out-root $RUNS, same prompt-hash refusal, one-job-at-a-time and dry-run behaviour. `job_total` for ad5/ad6 is the line count of its ids file (fall back to 48), and `job_raw` points at the run's raw dir.
Refuse `start ad5` / `start ad6` when its ids file is missing or empty with a clear message (an empty file means nothing remains: print 'nothing to do' and exit 0).

Extend tests/py/test_imp_ops.py (dry-run command table, missing ids file refusal, empty ids file) and document the jobs in docs/14 section 3 plus README.md, INDEX.md, NEXT-STEPS.md and ralph/README.md (imp-3, imp-ops-3).
criteria: `IMP_OPS_DRY=1 start ad5` prints the command with --ids-file=runs/imp/adaptive/ids_after_s4.txt once the file exists (asserted)
Missing and empty ids files behave as specified (asserted)
